event.politics_documentary.res0: The crew gets total unfiltered access. The footage is unflattering, viral, and impossible to walk back. New contracts pay 20% less for 7 days.
event.politics_documentary.res1: Only carefully curated footage gets released. The documentary looks great; it also barely resembles reality.
event.politics_documentary.res2: Cameras are banned from the site outright. The crew leaves and makes a documentary about being banned instead.
event.politics_documentary.title: Documentary
event.politics_eco_blockade.desc: "Rocks Have Feelings Too" eco-blockade. Politics finds its way to your pit.
event.politics_eco_blockade.res0: A negotiated settlement funds a wetland restoration project nearby. The blockade lifts, cordially.
event.politics_eco_blockade.res1: Bulldozers clear the blockade by force. Footage of the clearing outlives the blockade by years. Lawsuit events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.politics_eco_blockade.res2: A glossy PR campaign about 'rocks and feelings' runs in the regional press. It changes minds mildly, at best.
event.politics_eco_blockade.title: Eco Blockade
event.politics_efficiency_expert.desc: Government "efficiency expert" assigned. A government official has taken notice of your operation.
event.politics_efficiency_expert.res0: The expert's full restructuring plan gets implemented. Efficient on paper; miserable on the ground. Crews work 20% faster for 48 hours. Morale falls by 2 per hour for 12 hours.
event.politics_efficiency_expert.res1: The expert gets quietly distracted with a lavish 'fact-finding' trip instead of touching the org chart.
event.politics_efficiency_expert.res2: The expert's actually reasonable suggestions get implemented. Costly, and genuinely helpful for once. Crews work 20% faster for 48 hours.
event.politics_efficiency_expert.title: Efficiency Expert
event.politics_election.desc: Election: pro-mining vs anti-mining candidate. The political landscape shifts once more.
event.politics_election.res0: The pro-mining candidate's campaign gets a generous, deniable boost. New contracts pay 15% more for 7 days.
event.politics_election.res1: The anti-mining candidate's campaign gets funded instead, as a hedge and a good-faith gesture.
event.politics_election.res2: Nobody's campaign gets touched. The outcome is left entirely, nervously, to the voters.
event.politics_election.res2_alt: Staying neutral backfires — the anti-mining slate wins comfortably, citing your silence as proof of guilt.
event.politics_election.title: Election
event.politics_ev_mandate.desc: Government mandates electric vehicles. Politics finds its way to your pit.
event.politics_ev_mandate.res0: The entire haul fleet converts to electric. Quiet, clean, and extraordinarily expensive up front. Upkeep costs 15% less for 7 days.
event.politics_ev_mandate.res1: Compliance gets quietly delayed through the right channels. The diesel fleet keeps rolling, for now. Hauling is suspended for 24 hours.
event.politics_ev_mandate.res2: A hybrid fleet splits the difference. Half the emissions cut, half the invoice avoided.
event.politics_ev_mandate.title: Ev Mandate
event.politics_explosive_ban.desc: New regulation bans favorite explosive. Politics finds its way to your pit.
event.politics_explosive_ban.res0: Operations comply and switch to the newly approved explosive. Slower, cleaner, regulator-friendly.
event.politics_explosive_ban.res1: The banned explosive keeps being used, quietly, past the deadline. Inspectors are paid to look elsewhere. Blasting is banned for 24 hours.
event.politics_explosive_ban.res2: A lobbying push secures a temporary exemption. The clock is now ticking on borrowed time. Explosives cost 25% more for 7 days.
event.politics_explosive_ban.title: Explosive Ban
event.politics_explosive_embargo.desc: Republic of Boomistan embargoes explosives. The regulatory environment is changing.
event.politics_explosive_embargo.res0: A full stockpile is purchased at premium prices before the embargo bites. The warehouse now doubles as a bunker. Explosives cost 15% less for 7 days.
event.politics_explosive_embargo.res1: A black-market supplier fills the gap, no questions asked and no paperwork issued. Mafia events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.politics_explosive_embargo.res2: Operations switch to a locally approved alternative explosive. Slightly weaker, entirely legal. Output drops 20% for 48 hours.
event.politics_explosive_embargo.title: Explosive Embargo
event.politics_explosive_tariff.desc: New tariff on imported explosives. External forces are at play.
event.politics_explosive_tariff.res0: The tariff is paid in full, on time, without complaint filed anywhere official. Explosives cost 25% more for 7 days.
event.politics_explosive_tariff.res1: A loophole is found and exploited. The customs office remains unaware, for now. Lawsuit events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.politics_explosive_tariff.res2: A full switch to a local supplier avoids the tariff entirely, at real cost to the supply chain.
event.politics_explosive_tariff.title: Explosive Tariff
event.politics_gov_subsidy.desc: Government subsidy available (with strings). External forces are at play.
event.politics_gov_subsidy.res0: The no-strings subsidy is taken in full. Environmental oversight quietly relaxes to match the new budget. Lawsuit events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.politics_gov_subsidy.res1: The green-conditions subsidy is accepted. Smaller check, cleaner conscience, actual compliance paperwork.
event.politics_gov_subsidy.res2: The subsidy is declined altogether. Nobody owes anybody anything, which has its own quiet value.
event.politics_gov_subsidy.title: Gov Subsidy
event.politics_heritage_listing.desc: Mining heritage listed (can't blast certain areas). External forces are at play.
event.politics_heritage_listing.res0: The heritage listing is respected in full. Heritage markers go up and the crew is told to tread carefully around certain areas. Blasting is banned for 48 hours.
event.politics_heritage_listing.res1: The listing gets quietly delisted through a friendly official. The area reopens to blasting shortly after.
event.politics_heritage_listing.res2: A small heritage museum is built on-site instead, letting the mine keep both its history and its permit.
event.politics_heritage_listing.title: Heritage Listing
event.politics_insurance_hike.desc: Insurance company doubles premiums. A government official has taken notice of your operation.
event.politics_insurance_hike.res0: The doubled premium is paid without complaint. Expensive, but coverage stays intact.
event.politics_insurance_hike.res1: A shadier, cheaper insurer takes the policy instead. The fine print is worse than anyone bothered to read. Lawsuit events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.politics_insurance_hike.res2: A full safety overhaul earns a genuine discount from the insurer. Expensive now, cheaper for years after. Upkeep costs 15% less for 7 days. $250 leaves the account every day for 14 days.
event.politics_insurance_hike.title: Insurance Hike
event.politics_ipo_opportunity.desc: Mining company IPO opportunity. External forces are at play.
event.politics_ipo_opportunity.res0: The company goes public. A huge cash injection arrives, along with shareholders who now expect answers.
event.politics_ipo_opportunity.res1: The IPO is passed on entirely. The company stays private, small, and answerable to nobody but itself.
event.politics_ipo_opportunity.res2: A partial share sale raises decent capital without giving up full control. Lawsuit events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.politics_ipo_opportunity.title: Ipo Opportunity
event.politics_land_auction.desc: Mining rights auction for adjacent land. External forces are at play.
event.politics_land_auction.res0: The adjacent land is won at auction, outright and expensively. The pit's footprint grows overnight.
event.politics_land_auction.res1: The auction is skipped entirely. The adjacent land goes to a competitor, quietly and without incident.
event.politics_land_auction.res2: A joint-venture bid splits the winning cost and, in theory, the land's management.
event.politics_land_auction.res2_alt: The joint-venture partner reneges on the management split right after the auction closes.
event.politics_land_auction.title: Land Auction
event.politics_land_claim.desc: Mining rights dispute — ancestral land claim. A government official has taken notice of your operation.
event.politics_land_claim.res0: A fair settlement is reached with the ancestral claimants — real compensation, real recognition.
event.politics_land_claim.res1: A legal loophole voids the claim on a technicality. Cheap, fast, and reputationally toxic. Lawsuit events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.politics_land_claim.res2: A shared-stewardship agreement splits management of the disputed land. Slower, fairer, genuinely workable. A charge of $600 hits the books every day for 7 days.
event.politics_land_claim.title: Land Claim
event.politics_lobbyist.desc: Mining lobbyist offers "partnership". Politics finds its way to your pit.
event.politics_lobbyist.res0: The full lobbyist deal is signed. Cash flows in; so does a level of political obligation nobody wrote down. Politics events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.politics_lobbyist.res1: The partnership is declined. The lobbyist leaves unimpressed; the ecology score ticks up slightly out of relief.
event.politics_lobbyist.res2: A smaller 'favor' is accepted instead of the full deal. Modest cash, modest strings attached.
event.politics_lobbyist.title: Lobbyist
event.politics_mayor_antimine.desc: Local mayor running on "shut down the mine". External forces are at play.
event.politics_mayor_antimine.res0: The mayor's opponent gets a generous, untraceable campaign donation.
event.politics_mayor_antimine.res1: A genuine green PR push launches — real projects, real photos, real (if modest) results.
event.politics_mayor_antimine.res2: Nothing is done. The anti-mine mayor wins comfortably, and the fight moves to their office.
event.politics_mayor_antimine.title: Mayor Antimine
event.politics_mayor_wins.desc: You sat out the campaign, and the anti-mine mayor won in a landslide. Politics finds its way to your pit.
event.politics_mayor_wins.res0: The mine complies fully with the new mayor's restrictions. Expensive, legal, and genuinely cleaner. Blasting is banned for 48 hours.
event.politics_mayor_wins.res1: A lobbying push aims to overturn the restrictions at the regional level, corruption included.
event.politics_mayor_wins.res2: Operations relocate entirely to a friendlier jurisdiction. Everything stops for 24 hours while the move happens. Drastic, expensive, and a fresh start.
event.politics_mayor_wins.res3: A quiet 'negotiation' with the new mayor smooths over the restrictions considerably.
event.politics_mayor_wins.title: Mayor Wins
event.politics_meteor.desc: Meteor heading toward the mine (rare, fantastical). External forces are at play.
event.politics_meteor.res0: A full evacuation empties the mine well before impact. Costly, and nobody is anywhere near the crater. All work on site halts for 12 hours.
event.politics_meteor.res1: Nobody moves. The meteor's trajectory is trusted to miss, and mostly it does not go well.
event.politics_meteor.res1_alt: The meteor turns out to be laced with a genuinely rare ore. A terrifying, extremely profitable near miss.
event.politics_meteor.res2: The meteor is blasted apart mid-approach before it reaches the surface. A gamble that pays off cleanly.
event.politics_meteor.res2_alt: The intercept blast fails to fully break up the meteor. It still hits, smaller but not harmless.
event.politics_meteor.title: Meteor
event.politics_mine_tourism.desc: Tourism board wants mine tours. The political landscape shifts once more.
event.politics_mine_tourism.res0: Public mine tours open for business. Revenue rises; so does foot traffic near active machinery. An employee is hurt in the chaos.
event.politics_mine_tourism.res0_alt: Public mine tours open for business. Revenue rises; so does foot traffic near active machinery. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.politics_mine_tourism.res1: The offer is declined. The mine stays exactly as unvisited and exactly as safe as before.
event.politics_mine_tourism.res2: A small VIP-only tour program launches instead of general admission. Fewer visitors, fewer incidents.
event.politics_mine_tourism.title: Mine Tourism
event.politics_mining_ban_debate.desc: Parliament debates banning open-pit mining. A government official has taken notice of your operation.
event.politics_mining_ban_debate.res0: A full lobbying campaign floods parliament with reports, dinners, and carefully worded studies.
event.politics_mining_ban_debate.res1: No lobbying is done. The debate proceeds to an actual vote, unimpeded and unpurchased.
event.politics_mining_ban_debate.res2: Key politicians are bought outright before the debate even concludes. Blunt, expensive, effective.
event.politics_mining_ban_debate.title: Mining Ban Debate
event.politics_mining_ban_vote.desc: With no lobbying done, the debate has reached an actual vote. The political landscape shifts once more.
event.politics_mining_ban_vote.res0: An emergency lobbying blitz swings the vote in the mine's favor, at enormous expense.
event.politics_mining_ban_vote.res0_alt: The lobbying blitz fails to change enough votes. The partial restrictions pass anyway.
event.politics_mining_ban_vote.res1: A partial ban gets accepted: for 60 hours everyone works at 40% reduced speed rather than fighting it entirely.
event.politics_mining_ban_vote.res2: Key parliament members get bribed directly ahead of the vote. Blasting is banned for 24 hours.
event.politics_mining_ban_vote.title: Mining Ban Vote
event.politics_mining_cartel.desc: Mining cartel formed. The political landscape shifts once more.
event.politics_mining_cartel.res0: The cartel invitation is accepted. Prices stay comfortably fixed; so does everyone's growing discomfort with the arrangement. New contracts pay 15% more for 7 days.
event.politics_mining_cartel.res1: The cartel is refused outright. Competing on the open market is expensive, and considerably more honest. New contracts pay 20% less for 7 days.
event.politics_mining_cartel.res2: A double game is played — publicly declining while quietly gathering intelligence on their pricing.
event.politics_mining_cartel.title: Mining Cartel
event.politics_mining_expo.desc: International mining expo invitation. A government official has taken notice of your operation.
event.politics_mining_expo.res0: A booth is set up at the international expo. Modest foot traffic, a few decent leads. A lucrative special contract lands on the board.
event.politics_mining_expo.res1: The invitation is declined. The expo happens without the mine, which nobody there seems to mind either.
event.politics_mining_expo.res2: A keynote slot is secured and delivered flawlessly, turning heads across the industry.
event.politics_mining_expo.res2_alt: The keynote slot happens, but the speech falls flat. Polite applause, no real follow-up interest.
event.politics_mining_expo.title: Mining Expo
event.politics_mining_human_right.desc: Neighboring country declares mining a human right. The political landscape shifts once more.
event.politics_mining_human_right.res0: An influx of cheap cross-border labor arrives overnight. Payroll shrinks; so does everyone's job security. A new driller signs on at no cost. Wages fall 15% for 7 days.
event.politics_mining_human_right.res1: The declaration is ignored entirely. Nothing changes, which everyone quietly appreciates.
event.politics_mining_human_right.res2: New immigrant workers are hired through proper channels, at fair wages. Costlier, and considerably better for everyone's conscience. A new driller signs on at no cost. Wages rise 15% for 7 days.
event.politics_mining_human_right.title: Mining Human Right
event.politics_minister_visit.desc: Minister of Mines visiting. External forces are at play.
event.politics_minister_visit.res0: A full red-carpet tour is staged — polished equipment, briefed workers, catered lunch. The minister leaves impressed. A lucrative special contract lands on the board.
event.politics_minister_visit.res1: The minister gets the honest, unpolished tour. It is not flattering, but nobody can say they lied. New contracts pay 20% less for 7 days.
event.politics_minister_visit.res2: A carefully staged 'model section' of the mine is built just for the visit. The rest of the pit stays exactly as it was.
event.politics_minister_visit.title: Minister Visit
event.politics_nationalization.desc: Fictional country nationalizes all mines. The regulatory environment is changing.
event.politics_nationalization.res0: The nationalization order is complied with in full. The mine becomes state property, cleanly and legally.
event.politics_nationalization.res1: Assets get quietly moved offshore before the paperwork clears. The state inherits considerably less than it expected. Lawsuit events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.politics_nationalization.res2: The mine converts to a worker cooperative instead, dodging nationalization on a technicality everyone quietly celebrates. Wages rise 10% permanently.
event.politics_nationalization.title: Nationalization
event.politics_neighbor_collapse.desc: Neighboring mine collapses. The regulatory environment is changing.
event.politics_neighbor_collapse.res0: A rescue team is dispatched immediately. Costly, and it earns the kind of goodwill that money usually can't buy. Morale rises by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.politics_neighbor_collapse.res1: Their clients get poached while rescue crews are still on site. Profitable, and not something to put on a brochure. A lucrative special contract lands on the board.
event.politics_neighbor_collapse.res2: A voluntary safety audit is commissioned in response. Cheap insurance against being next.
event.politics_neighbor_collapse.title: Neighbor Collapse
event.politics_ngo_partnership.desc: Environmental NGO offers partnership. The political landscape shifts once more.
event.politics_ngo_partnership.res0: A genuine partnership forms with the environmental NGO. Real oversight, real improvements, real cost.
event.politics_ngo_partnership.res1: The partnership offer is rejected. The NGO publishes a report about the mine anyway, unflattering and thorough. New contracts pay 30% less for 10 days.
event.politics_ngo_partnership.res2: A token gesture — a small donation, a nice photo — satisfies the NGO's press release, if not its actual mission.
event.politics_ngo_partnership.title: Ngo Partnership
event.politics_ore_crash.desc: International ore price crash. The regulatory environment is changing.
event.politics_ore_crash.res0: Existing contracts are honored at a steep loss. Reputation stays intact; the balance sheet does not.
event.politics_ore_crash.res1: Contracts get quietly renegotiated through less-than-official channels. Cheaper, riskier, deniable. A running contract is cancelled.
event.politics_ore_crash.res1_alt: Contracts get quietly renegotiated through less-than-official channels. Cheaper, riskier, deniable. There is no open contract to cancel, so the client has nothing to walk away from.
event.politics_ore_crash.res2: Layoffs absorb the price crash. The balance sheet recovers; morale does not. An employee hands in their notice and is gone by lunch. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.politics_ore_crash.res2_alt: Layoffs absorb the price crash. The balance sheet recovers; morale does not. There is nobody left to quit, so nobody does. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.politics_ore_crash.title: Ore Crash
event.politics_reality_tv.desc: Reality TV show wants to film at mine. A government official has taken notice of your operation.
event.politics_reality_tv.res0: Full camera access is granted. Ratings soar; so does the accident count, conveniently edited out of the broadcast.
event.politics_reality_tv.res1: Filming is declined outright. The mine stays boring and, blessedly, off television.
event.politics_reality_tv.res2: A tightly controlled filming schedule is negotiated. Fewer dramatic shots, fewer actual dramas.
event.politics_reality_tv.title: Reality Tv
event.politics_safety_summit.desc: International mining safety summit. A government official has taken notice of your operation.
event.politics_safety_summit.res0: The full delegation attends the safety summit. New protocols come home and actually get implemented.
event.politics_safety_summit.res1: The summit is skipped entirely. Safety practices stay exactly as outdated as before. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.politics_safety_summit.res2: A single delegate is sent instead of the full team. Some useful notes come back, secondhand.
event.politics_safety_summit.title: Safety Summit
event.politics_sanctions.desc: International sanctions affect ore exports. The regulatory environment is changing.
event.politics_sanctions.res0: New buyers are found outside the sanctioned markets. It takes time and costs plenty, but the ore keeps moving. New contracts pay 20% less for 7 days.
event.politics_sanctions.res1: A smuggling route around the sanctions turns a tidy profit, quietly, in cash.
event.politics_sanctions.res2: Exports pivot to the domestic market instead. Lower margins, zero exposure to international sanctions. New contracts pay 30% less for 10 days.
event.politics_sanctions.title: Sanctions
event.politics_stock_bubble.desc: Mining stock market bubble. External forces are at play.
event.politics_stock_bubble.res0: Heavy investment rides the mining stock bubble to a spectacular payout.
event.politics_stock_bubble.res0_alt: The bubble bursts mid-ride. The investment evaporates along with a large chunk of the treasury.
event.politics_stock_bubble.res1: A cautious, modest investment yields a small but reliable return. Nothing dramatic, nothing lost either.
event.politics_stock_bubble.res2: The market is ignored entirely. Whatever happens to the bubble, the mine's fortunes stay untouched.
event.politics_stock_bubble.title: Stock Bubble
event.politics_tax_audit.desc: Surprise tax audit. The political landscape shifts once more.
event.politics_tax_audit.res0: The audit runs its full, brutal course. Every receipt since founding gets examined; the fine is enormous.
event.politics_tax_audit.res1: The books get 'creatively' restructured overnight. The audit concludes early, satisfied with numbers that do not quite exist. Lawsuit events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.politics_tax_audit.res2: Partial disclosure is offered — enough to look cooperative, not enough to look guilty. $600 leaves the account every day for 7 days.
event.politics_tax_audit.title: Tax Audit
event.politics_tax_reform.desc: Government announces mining tax reform. Politics finds its way to your pit.
event.politics_tax_reform.res0: The mine complies fully with the new tax reform. Expensive, transparent, and unexpectedly good for the ecology score.
event.politics_tax_reform.res1: Profits get routed through a freshly opened offshore shell. The reform, on paper, barely applies anymore.
event.politics_tax_reform.res2: A lobbying campaign against the reform launches. Expensive, and its success is far from guaranteed. $250 leaves the account every day for 14 days.
event.politics_tax_reform.title: Tax Reform
event.politics_trade_war.desc: Trade war with Explosistan. The regulatory environment is changing.
event.politics_trade_war.res0: Tariffs are absorbed and a stockpile is built to ride out the trade war. Expensive insurance against politics. Explosives cost 15% less for 7 days.
event.politics_trade_war.res1: A smuggling route around the tariffs opens up. Cheaper supplies, considerably higher legal exposure. Mafia events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.politics_trade_war.res2: A domestic supplier replaces the foreign one. Costs more up front, and quietly improves the ecology score. Explosives cost 25% more for 7 days.
event.politics_trade_war.title: Trade War
event.politics_un_inspector.desc: UN inspector surprise visit. The regulatory environment is changing.
event.politics_un_inspector.res0: An emergency cleanup crew scrubs the site spotless overnight. The inspector finds a model operation. Every crew downs tools for 12 hours.
event.politics_un_inspector.res1: No cleanup happens. The inspector files a formal UN citation, which follows the mine for years. Blasting is banned for 24 hours.
event.politics_un_inspector.res2: An envelope resolves the inspection faster than any cleanup crew ever could.
event.politics_un_inspector.title: Un Inspector
event.politics_viral_hashtag.desc: Social media campaign against your mine. External forces are at play.
event.politics_viral_hashtag.res0: A full PR blitz counters the hashtag within days. The story fades from feeds almost as fast as it appeared.
event.politics_viral_hashtag.res1: No response is issued. The hashtag trends for a full news cycle, unchallenged. New contracts pay 30% less for 10 days.
event.politics_viral_hashtag.res2: An influencer is hired to post something reassuring. It works, mostly on people who were never worried.
event.politics_viral_hashtag.title: Viral Hashtag
event.politics_whistleblower.desc: Whistleblower leaks internal documents. Politics finds its way to your pit.
event.politics_whistleblower.res0: A public transparency pledge is issued, backed by real changes. Corruption levels actually drop.
event.politics_whistleblower.res1: The whistleblower is quietly paid to disappear from the story. It works, at a real cost to morale. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.politics_whistleblower.res2: A full internal reform program launches, addressing exactly what the leaked documents exposed.
event.politics_whistleblower.title: Whistleblower
event.traffic_jam.desc: Drivers and walkers are stuck in a knot at a chokepoint. Nobody is moving, everyone is honking and muttering.
event.traffic_jam.res0: Everyone in the knot is re-routed to a different spot. No cost, and traffic starts moving again within minutes.
event.traffic_jam.res1: The ramp is ordered wider to prevent future jams. Expensive, and it fixes the bottleneck for good once dug.
event.traffic_jam.res2: The jam is left to sort itself out. Eventually it does, at the cost of a very long, very honked afternoon.
event.traffic_jam.res1_alt: The ramp cannot be widened right now: it is already the widest, is already being widened, cannot be dug, or the mine cannot afford it. Nothing is spent, and the jam stays.
event.traffic_jam.title: Traffic Jam
event.tutorial_synergy_consultant.desc: A man in a suit that costs more than your entire operation clicks a PowerPoint remote...
event.tutorial_synergy_consultant.opt2: I'll pay you in exposure and company equity.
event.tutorial_synergy_consultant.res0: He's hired on the spot. Three weeks later he delivers a two-hundred-slide deck recommending you dig holes in the ground. Invoice attached.
event.tutorial_synergy_consultant.res1: He leaves without a word, but not before slipping an embossed business card under the office door.
event.tutorial_synergy_consultant.res2: He accepts payment in 'exposure and equity' instantly, which should probably worry you more than it does.
event.tutorial_synergy_consultant.title: A Wild Consultant Appears!
event.union_anthem.desc: Company anthem demand. The workers' committee is at your door again.
event.union_anthem.res0: A full company anthem is composed and performed at the morning briefing. It somehow has a key change.
event.union_anthem.res1: No anthem. Morning briefings remain anthem-free and considerably shorter.
event.union_anthem.res2: A karaoke night is offered instead of a formal anthem. Someone improvises one anyway, off-key.
event.union_anthem.title: Anthem
event.union_board_seat.desc: Seat on the "board" (literal wooden board). Workers have gathered outside your office.
event.union_board_seat.res0: A literal wooden board seat is installed at the edge of the meeting table, with full voting rights.
event.union_board_seat.res1: You deny them a seat on the board, literal or otherwise. A quiet grudge is added to the ledger. Union events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.union_board_seat.res2: A folding chair is set up just outside the boardroom door instead. Symbolic, and everyone knows it.
event.union_board_seat.title: Board Seat
event.union_book_club.desc: Unauthorized book club during shifts. The workers' committee is at your door again.
event.union_book_club.res0: Management officially sanctions the book club and even buys the paperbacks. Productivity dips fifteen minutes a day. Everyone gets a proper rest and starts the next shift fully recharged.
event.union_book_club.res1: The book club is banned outright. Copies of the offending novel now circulate underground. Union events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.union_book_club.res2: The club is allowed to meet, but only on unpaid lunch breaks. A wobbly compromise, gratefully accepted.
event.union_book_club.title: Book Club
event.union_burial_ground.desc: Ancient burial ground discovery. Another day, another union demand.
event.union_burial_ground.res0: A licensed archaeologist is brought in to survey the site properly. The dig pauses, respectfully and expensively. Drilling is banned for 12 hours.
event.union_burial_ground.res1: The site is blasted through regardless. The mine acquires a reputation nobody wanted, and a nickname that sticks. An employee hands in their notice and is gone by lunch.
event.union_burial_ground.res1_alt: The site is blasted through regardless. The mine acquires a reputation nobody wanted, and a nickname that sticks. There is nobody left to quit, so nobody does.
event.union_burial_ground.res2: A small roadside gift shop is set up over the discovery, tastefully, mostly.
event.union_burial_ground.res2_alt: The gift shop becomes an unexpected tourist trap. It turns a profit, at some cost to the site's dignity.
event.union_burial_ground.title: Burial Ground
event.union_casual_friday.desc: Casual Friday in a mine. Another day, another union demand.
event.union_casual_friday.res0: Casual Friday is approved. Sandals near heavy machinery turn out to be exactly as unsafe as it sounds.
event.union_casual_friday.res1: Branded casual-wear PPE ships in — steel-toe sneakers, soft-shell vests. Everyone looks relaxed and remains compliant.
event.union_casual_friday.res2: Uniform policy stays rigid. The suggestion box gets a strongly worded memo about 'professionalism'. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_casual_friday.title: Casual Friday
event.union_coffee_uprising.desc: Workers demand artisanal espresso machine. Workers have gathered outside your office.
event.union_coffee_uprising.res0: The imported espresso machine arrives, gleaming and absurdly loud. Morale rises with the crema. Morale rises by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_coffee_uprising.res1: You remind them coffee is a privilege, not a right. The picket line disagrees. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_coffee_uprising.res2: A jar of instant granules and a hand-written 'Barista Corner' sign settles it, barely.
event.union_coffee_uprising.title: Coffee Uprising
event.union_company_band.desc: Workers want a company band. The suggestion box is overflowing again.
event.union_company_band.res0: A full company orchestra forms, complete with a tuba. Rehearsals carry for kilometers.
event.union_company_band.res1: No band. The break room radio remains the sole musical outlet, and it is universally hated. Crews work 20% slower for 48 hours.
event.union_company_band.res2: An informal lunchtime jam session is permitted instead. Two guitars, one off-key harmonica, genuine joy.
event.union_company_band.title: Company Band
event.union_corner_office.desc: Union rep demands corner office in the pit. Another day, another union demand.
event.union_corner_office.res0: A prefab office with a window goes up at the pit's edge, officially for the union rep. Everyone wants one now.
event.union_corner_office.res1: You refuse outright. The rep starts quietly cataloguing every other perk you've ever handed a manager. Union events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.union_corner_office.res2: A 'consulting stipend' appears on the rep's paycheck. The corner-office demand quietly disappears.
event.union_corner_office.title: Corner Office
event.union_cursed_hole.desc: Refuse to work near "cursed" drill hole. Another day, another union demand.
event.union_cursed_hole.res0: A registered exorcist is hired for the afternoon. The invoice lists it as 'geological consulting'.
event.union_cursed_hole.res1: The hole stays cursed, officially unacknowledged. Crews route around it, less carefully than they should. Drilling is banned for 12 hours.
event.union_cursed_hole.res2: The drill plan is quietly redrawn around the cursed coordinates. Nobody asks why; everyone is relieved.
event.union_cursed_hole.title: Cursed Hole
event.union_drills_realistic.desc: Safety drills too realistic. The suggestion box is overflowing again.
event.union_drills_realistic.res0: Safety drills are toned down to something survivable. Attendance and morale both improve. Morale rises by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_drills_realistic.res1: Drills stay as realistic as the real thing, which is exactly the problem everyone is complaining about. One employee ends up in the infirmary.
event.union_drills_realistic.res1_alt: Drills stay as realistic as the real thing, which is exactly the problem everyone is complaining about. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.union_drills_realistic.res2: Drills are quietly cancelled altogether. Nobody panics anymore, mostly because nobody practices anymore either.
event.union_drills_realistic.title: Drills Realistic
event.union_eco_committee.desc: Environmental sub-committee. The workers' committee is at your door again.
event.union_eco_committee.res0: An employee-run eco-committee is chartered with a real budget. It starts composting the cafeteria scraps within a week.
event.union_eco_committee.res1: The committee is denied. Someone starts a rogue recycling bin behind the warehouse anyway. Crews work 20% slower for 48 hours.
event.union_eco_committee.res2: A modest set of recycling bins appears by the cafeteria. It is not a committee, but it is something.
event.union_eco_committee.title: Eco Committee
event.union_ergo_chairs.desc: Ergonomic chairs for the pit. Workers have gathered outside your office.
event.union_ergo_chairs.res0: Reclining ergonomic chairs are bolted next to the drill stations. Lumbar support at the edge of an open pit.
event.union_ergo_chairs.res1: The metal folding stools stay. So does the complaining. Output drops 20% for 48 hours.
event.union_ergo_chairs.title: Ergo Chairs
event.union_food_trucks.desc: Food truck festival. The union rep is tapping their foot impatiently.
event.union_food_trucks.res0: A full food-truck festival takes over the parking lot for a day. The smell of tacos reaches the neighboring village. Everyone gets a proper rest and starts the next shift fully recharged.
event.union_food_trucks.res1: No festival. The vending machine's expired sandwiches remain the only lunch option.
event.union_food_trucks.res2: The vending machines get restocked with slightly fresher options. A modest, edible improvement.
event.union_food_trucks.title: Food Trucks
event.union_ghost_backpay.desc: Ghost unionized, demands back pay (rare, fantastical). The union rep is tapping their foot impatiently.
event.union_ghost_backpay.res0: The mine settles the deceased employee's back pay in full, with interest. The haunting stops; the accountants have questions.
event.union_ghost_backpay.res1: You refuse to pay a ghost. The ghost is unimpressed and considerably less cooperative. All work on site halts for 12 hours.
event.union_ghost_backpay.res2: A discreet exorcism is arranged and quietly filed under miscellaneous consulting fees.
event.union_ghost_backpay.res3: You promote the ghost to Safety Officer Emeritus. HR is baffled, but the paperwork somehow clears.
event.union_ghost_backpay.res3_alt: The promotion paperwork gets lost in committee. A smaller severance payment quiets things down instead.
event.union_ghost_backpay.title: Ghost Backpay
event.union_golden_hour.desc: Golden hour selfie refusal. The workers' committee is at your door again.
event.union_golden_hour.res0: A scheduled 'golden hour' selfie break is added near sunset. Productivity dips five minutes a day for better lighting.
event.union_golden_hour.res1: The request is denied. Selfies get taken anyway, mid-shift, with worse lighting and worse timing. Output drops 20% for 48 hours.
event.union_golden_hour.res2: A ring light is provided instead of a scheduled break. Content quality improves; the schedule stays intact.
event.union_golden_hour.title: Golden Hour
event.union_hat_color.desc: Hard hat color complaint. The suggestion box is overflowing again.
event.union_hat_color.res0: A rainbow of custom hard-hat colors ships in. Team identification improves by accident.
event.union_hat_color.res1: Regulation yellow stays regulation yellow. A quiet, ongoing sulk follows. Morale falls by 2 per hour for 12 hours.
event.union_hat_color.title: Hat Color
event.union_hazard_emotional.desc: Emotional proximity to explosions. Workers have gathered outside your office.
event.union_hazard_emotional.res0: An 'emotional proximity' stipend of $400 is added to the payroll every day for 7 days, then quietly lapses.
event.union_hazard_emotional.res1: You explain that fear is not a line item. The complaint gets filed, loudly, again next week. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_hazard_emotional.res2: A box of earplugs is relabeled 'feelings dampeners' and handed out. It is, technically, still earplugs.
event.union_hazard_emotional.title: Hazard Emotional
event.union_heated_seats.desc: Heated toilet seats ultimatum. Another day, another union demand.
event.union_heated_seats.res0: Heated toilet seats are installed throughout the site. A strange hill to die on, but the crews are thrilled.
event.union_heated_seats.res1: The demand is refused. A slowdown threat follows almost immediately, over toilet seats. Every crew downs tools for 12 hours.
event.union_heated_seats.res2: Basic stick-on seat warmers are provided instead of proper heated fixtures. A cheap, lukewarm peace.
event.union_heated_seats.title: Heated Seats
event.union_karaoke_demand.desc: Mandatory karaoke night. The union rep is tapping their foot impatiently.
event.union_karaoke_demand.res0: You rent a fog machine and a mediocre PA system. Wednesdays now end in power ballads audible from the village.
event.union_karaoke_demand.res1: No karaoke. The suggestion box fills with strongly worded song requests instead. Union events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.union_karaoke_demand.res2: A cheap secondhand microphone and a strict Wednesday-only schedule keep everyone just satisfied enough.
event.union_karaoke_demand.title: Karaoke Demand
event.union_lunch_quality.desc: Lunch menu quality complaints. Workers have gathered outside your office.
event.union_lunch_quality.res0: A genuine chef is hired. Lunch menus now list provenance. Nobody mentions the payroll line item. Crews work 20% faster for 48 hours.
event.union_lunch_quality.res1: The cafeteria stays exactly as bad. Tupperware imports from home spike. One employee quits on the spot.
event.union_lunch_quality.res1_alt: The cafeteria stays exactly as bad. Tupperware imports from home spike. There is nobody left to quit, so nobody does.
event.union_lunch_quality.res2: Taco Tuesday is instituted. It solves nothing structurally, but everyone likes tacos.
event.union_lunch_quality.title: Lunch Quality
event.union_lunch_thief.desc: Lunch thief investigation. The workers' committee is at your door again.
event.union_lunch_thief.res0: Fridge cameras go up in the break room. The lunch thief is identified within the hour and quietly shamed.
event.union_lunch_thief.res1: No investigation. Sandwiches keep vanishing, and suspicion spreads faster than the theft itself. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_lunch_thief.res2: A private detective is hired for the case and cracks it within a day, to everyone's mild embarrassment.
event.union_lunch_thief.res2_alt: The private detective, deep undercover, eats someone's lunch during the investigation. The case remains open.
event.union_lunch_thief.title: Lunch Thief
event.union_mascot.desc: Company mascot demand. The suggestion box is overflowing again.
event.union_mascot.res0: A foam mascot named Rocky debuts at the gate. Morale ticks up; several children are terrified.
event.union_mascot.res1: No mascot. The suggestion box gets three separate hand-drawn mascot proposals anyway.
event.union_mascot.res2: A full animatronic mascot is commissioned. It waves. It occasionally malfunctions and screams. Morale rises by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_mascot.title: Mascot
event.union_meditation.desc: Meditation sessions between blasts. Another day, another union demand.
event.union_meditation.res0: Guided yoga sessions are scheduled between blasts. Downward dog, thirty meters from a detonation. Morale rises by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_meditation.res1: No meditation program. Stress levels return to their usual pre-blast baseline.
event.union_meditation.res2: A short breathing-exercise handout is distributed instead. It is, at minimum, free and harmless.
event.union_meditation.title: Meditation
event.union_merch.desc: Company merchandise demand. Another day, another union demand.
event.union_merch.res0: Official branded hoodies and mugs ship in. Half the crew wears the hoodie to the next shift.
event.union_merch.res1: No merch. A worker starts printing bootleg mine T-shirts in their garage regardless.
event.union_merch.res2: A small batch of cheap, slightly crooked bootleg-style merch is quietly authorized instead.
event.union_merch.title: Merch
event.union_micro_rest.desc: Foreman micro-rest defense. Another day, another union demand.
event.union_micro_rest.res0: Nap pods are installed near the drill line. Five-minute breaks are now technically furnished. Everyone gets a proper rest and starts the next shift fully recharged.
event.union_micro_rest.res1: The foreman who banned micro-rests is fired for the trouble he caused. Morale improves out of spite. One manager quits on the spot.
event.union_micro_rest.res1_alt: The foreman who banned micro-rests is fired for the trouble he caused. Morale improves out of spite. There is nobody left to quit, so nobody does.
event.union_micro_rest.res2: A rotating siesta schedule is posted. Nobody follows it exactly, but everyone appreciates the gesture.
event.union_micro_rest.title: Micro Rest
event.union_miner_month.desc: Miner of the Month election. Another day, another union demand.
event.union_miner_month.res0: A 'Miner of the Month' plaque and a modest bonus are instituted. The ceremony is unexpectedly touching. Crews work 20% faster for 48 hours.
event.union_miner_month.res1: No award program. Recognition remains an entirely internal, entirely unspoken affair. Union events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.union_miner_month.res2: A cheap popularity-contest version runs instead — no bonus, just a sticker and simmering resentment.
event.union_miner_month.title: Miner Month
event.union_motivational_posters.desc: Protest against motivational posters. The union rep is tapping their foot impatiently.
event.union_motivational_posters.res0: Every 'Safety Is No Accident' poster comes down. The walls look bare and considerably less patronizing.
event.union_motivational_posters.res1: The posters stay up. So does the low hum of collective irritation. Output drops 30% for 36 hours.
event.union_motivational_posters.res2: Workers get to hang their own posters instead. Several are, unexpectedly, about the posters.
event.union_motivational_posters.title: Motivational Posters
event.union_music_complaint.desc: Anonymous music complaint. The suggestion box is overflowing again.
event.union_music_complaint.res0: A jukebox is installed in the break room, curated by nobody and blamed by everybody.
event.union_music_complaint.res1: No jukebox. The anonymous complaint escalates to a very specific, very loud complaint. Union events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.union_music_complaint.res2: An actual DJ is hired for lunch hour. The bass carries into the pit; nobody seems to mind.
event.union_music_complaint.title: Music Complaint
event.union_nap_room.desc: Nap Room. Workers have gathered outside your office.
event.union_nap_room.res0: A proper nap room opens — cots, blackout curtains, a strict no-snoring policy nobody enforces. Everyone gets a proper rest and starts the next shift fully recharged.
event.union_nap_room.res1: No nap room. Employees nap in vehicle cabs instead, which does nothing for anyone's insurance. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_nap_room.res2: Hammocks go up in a storage corner. Structurally questionable, surprisingly popular.
event.union_nap_room.title: Nap Room
event.union_newsletter.desc: Company newsletter demand. Workers have gathered outside your office.
event.union_newsletter.res0: An official company newsletter launches, complete with a masthead nobody asked for.
event.union_newsletter.res1: No newsletter. News continues to travel exclusively through the break-room rumor mill.
event.union_newsletter.res2: A gossip column sneaks into the newsletter's second issue. Readership triples overnight.
event.union_newsletter.title: Newsletter
event.union_noise_complaint.desc: Complaint about ambient explosion noise. Workers have gathered outside your office.
event.union_noise_complaint.res0: Industrial noise-cancelling headsets ship to every worker. The pit sounds the same; nobody hears it anymore.
event.union_noise_complaint.res1: Nothing changes. The blast schedule continues at full volume, as does the grumbling. Every crew downs tools for 12 hours.
event.union_noise_complaint.res2: A box of foam earplugs is distributed. It helps a little, mostly with the grumbling.
event.union_noise_complaint.title: Noise Complaint
event.union_overtime_revolt.desc: Demand end to 14-hour shifts. The suggestion box is overflowing again.
event.union_overtime_revolt.res0: Shifts drop to a humane length and you hire extra crews to cover it. Accident reports thin out. A new driller signs on at no cost.
event.union_overtime_revolt.res1: Fourteen-hour shifts continue. Fatigue turns muscle memory into guesswork near the drill rigs. Output drops 20% for 48 hours.
event.union_overtime_revolt.res2: Shifts trim by two hours — still brutal, but the union accepts it as a down payment.
event.union_overtime_revolt.title: Overtime Revolt
event.union_pet_day.desc: Bring-your-pet day. The workers' committee is at your door again.
event.union_pet_day.res0: Pets are welcomed into the active pit. Morale soars; so does the incident log involving a dog and a conveyor belt.
event.union_pet_day.res1: No pets on site, full stop. Several phone backgrounds change to cat photos in protest. Union events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.union_pet_day.res2: A pet-photo board goes up in the break room instead. Nobody gets bitten; everybody gets to see the dog.
event.union_pet_day.title: Pet Day
event.union_pet_rock_leave.desc: Pet rock maternity leave. The union rep is tapping their foot impatiently.
event.union_pet_rock_leave.res0: A designated pet rock nursery corner is set up in the break room, complete with tiny name tags.
event.union_pet_rock_leave.res1: No nursery. Pet rocks get left on desks, judging silently through the whole shift.
event.union_pet_rock_leave.res2: A shared cardboard box serves as makeshift rock daycare. It is, against all odds, taken very seriously.
event.union_pet_rock_leave.title: Pet Rock Leave
event.union_profit_sharing.desc: Workers demand profit sharing. The union rep is tapping their foot impatiently.
event.union_profit_sharing.res0: A profit-sharing payout lands. The checks are small but real, and morale climbs with them.
event.union_profit_sharing.res1: You explain that profits are for shareholders. The explanation does not go over well, and word gets around. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_profit_sharing.res2: Pizza Fridays are instituted instead of profit sharing. A cheaper, greasier substitute for equity.
event.union_profit_sharing.title: Profit Sharing
event.union_rename_blastzone.desc: Rename "blast zone" petition. The workers' committee is at your door again.
event.union_rename_blastzone.res0: The blast zone is officially rebranded 'Happy Zone'. The explosions remain unchanged.
event.union_rename_blastzone.res1: The name stays. So does the low-grade dread every time someone says it over the radio. Morale falls by 2 per hour for 12 hours.
event.union_rename_blastzone.res2: A focus group is convened to workshop alternatives. It settles on nothing and disbands.
event.union_rename_blastzone.title: Rename Blastzone
event.union_rename_explosives.desc: Rename explosives petition. The union rep is tapping their foot impatiently.
event.union_rename_explosives.res0: Explosives get gentler branding — 'boom units' instead of 'charges'. Safety perception improves, marginally.
event.union_rename_explosives.res1: The terminology stays clinical and terrifying. Everyone continues to say 'charge' with the same flinch.
event.union_rename_explosives.res2: A small euphemism handbook is printed for onboarding. It fools exactly nobody, but it is very polite.
event.union_rename_explosives.title: Rename Explosives
event.union_rep_secretary.desc: Union rep wants a secretary. The suggestion box is overflowing again.
event.union_rep_secretary.res0: The union rep gets an actual secretary. Meeting minutes are now typed, dated, and impossible to deny later. A new manager signs on at no cost.
event.union_rep_secretary.res1: You deny the request. The rep starts keeping their own meticulous, handwritten record of everything you say.
event.union_rep_secretary.res2: A cheap voice recorder is provided instead of a secretary. It captures everything, which later becomes a problem.
event.union_rep_secretary.title: Rep Secretary
event.union_retreat.desc: Company retreat planning. The union rep is tapping their foot impatiently.
event.union_retreat.res0: A full beach retreat is booked — flights, cocktails, a mandatory trust-fall exercise nobody enjoys but everyone remembers fondly.
event.union_retreat.res1: No retreat. The team-building budget quietly returns to the general fund. The most junior employee hands in their notice and is gone by lunch.
event.union_retreat.res1_alt: No retreat. The team-building budget quietly returns to the general fund. There is nobody left to quit, so nobody does.
event.union_retreat.res2: A camping trip substitutes for the beach resort. Tents leak; morale rises anyway.
event.union_retreat.title: Retreat
event.union_safety_helmets.desc: Workers refuse unflattering helmets. The workers' committee is at your door again.
event.union_safety_helmets.res0: Matte-black designer helmets ship in. They photograph beautifully and, incidentally, meet code.
event.union_safety_helmets.res1: You point out helmets protect skulls, not egos. Compliance drops along with morale. An employee hands in their notice and is gone by lunch.
event.union_safety_helmets.res1_alt: You point out helmets protect skulls, not egos. Compliance drops along with morale. There is nobody left to quit, so nobody does.
event.union_safety_helmets.res2: A full runway line of hard hats debuts in the break room — three colorways, zero irony.
event.union_safety_helmets.title: Safety Helmets
event.union_slowdown.desc: "Slow-down" protest (working at normal speed). The suggestion box is overflowing again.
event.union_slowdown.res0: Mandatory overtime is abolished outright. Output dips slightly; nobody collapses from exhaustion this month. Output drops 20% for 48 hours.
event.union_slowdown.res1: Overtime stays mandatory. Crews start working to rule, and safety margins shrink along with their patience. Crews work 30% slower for 36 hours.
event.union_slowdown.res2: Overtime is capped at a 'reasonable' level. Nobody agrees on what reasonable means, but the protest ends.
event.union_slowdown.title: Slowdown
event.union_strike_aftermath.desc: Every worker walked off site, and the strike is still going. The workers' committee is at your door again.
event.union_strike_aftermath.res0: The mine capitulates completely — retroactive raises, back pay, a brand-new ping-pong table. The picket line disbands. Wages rise 10% permanently.
event.union_strike_aftermath.res1: Scab labor gets hired to resume production. Output recovers; morale and safety both take a hit. A new driller signs on at no cost. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_strike_aftermath.res2: The mine closes 'for maintenance' as a stalling tactic. Nobody is fooled, but it buys a little time. Every crew downs tools for 12 hours.
event.union_strike_aftermath.title: Strike Aftermath
event.union_strike_threat.desc: General strike vote. Another day, another union demand.
event.union_strike_threat.res0: You cave completely — raises, back pay, an apology letter. The treasury groans; the picket signs come down. Wages rise 15% for 7 days.
event.union_strike_threat.res1: You call their bluff. Every single worker walks off site for 24 hours. This will not end here.
event.union_strike_threat.res2: An envelope changes hands under the table. The union boss develops sudden, expensive patience.
event.union_strike_threat.title: Strike Threat
event.union_suggestion_box.desc: Suggestion box (filled with complaints). Workers have gathered outside your office.
event.union_suggestion_box.res0: A proper suggestion box is installed, complete with a lock and a designated reader. Suggestions triple overnight.
event.union_suggestion_box.res1: No box. Complaints get shouted across the yard instead, which is somehow less efficient. Union events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.union_suggestion_box.res2: A shredder is quietly installed behind the box instead of a reader. Nobody notices for months.
event.union_suggestion_box.title: Suggestion Box
event.union_talent_show.desc: Talent show in the quarry. The union rep is tapping their foot impatiently.
event.union_talent_show.res0: A full stage, lighting rig, and open mic go up at the edge of the pit. The judging panel takes it very seriously. Everyone gets a proper rest and starts the next shift fully recharged.
event.union_talent_show.res1: No talent show. Morale drops in a key nobody can quite name. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_talent_show.res2: A modest lunchroom talent show, no stage, no lights — just three acts and polite applause.
event.union_talent_show.title: Talent Show
event.union_talking_rocks.desc: Rocks are speaking to a worker. The union rep is tapping their foot impatiently.
event.union_talking_rocks.res0: The worker is quietly designated 'rock whisperer' and reassigned to survey support. It works out unexpectedly well.
event.union_talking_rocks.res0_alt: The reassignment does not go well. The worker keeps hearing the rocks, now with company opinions.
event.union_talking_rocks.res1: A mandatory psych evaluation is ordered. The worker passes, resentfully, and never mentions the rocks again.
event.union_talking_rocks.res2: Survey equipment is dispatched to check the claim. The data comes back suspiciously, remarkably accurate.
event.union_talking_rocks.title: Talking Rocks
event.union_therapist.desc: Company therapist petition. The suggestion box is overflowing again.
event.union_therapist.res0: A licensed therapist joins payroll. Session notes remain confidential; the invoice does not. Everyone gets a proper rest and starts the next shift fully recharged.
event.union_therapist.res1: No therapist. Feelings continue to be processed the old-fashioned way, at the bar after shift. Output drops 20% for 48 hours.
event.union_therapist.res2: A stack of self-help paperbacks appears in the break room. Chapter one goes surprisingly fast.
event.union_therapist.title: Therapist
event.union_truck_parking.desc: Better parking spaces for haul trucks. The workers' committee is at your door again.
event.union_truck_parking.res0: Valet parking for haul trucks. A grown adult now parks forty-ton vehicles for a living. Upkeep costs 15% less for 7 days.
event.union_truck_parking.res1: Parking stays first-come, first-served chaos. Fender benders between forty-ton trucks remain a Tuesday occurrence. An employee is hurt in the chaos.
event.union_truck_parking.res1_alt: Parking stays first-come, first-served chaos. Fender benders between forty-ton trucks remain a Tuesday occurrence. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.union_truck_parking.res2: Assigned parking spots, painted and numbered. Nobody should fight over them; several people still do.
event.union_truck_parking.title: Truck Parking
event.union_tv_channel.desc: Break room TV channel war. The suggestion box is overflowing again.
event.union_tv_channel.res0: A second TV goes up in the break room, ending the remote-control standoff — mostly.
event.union_tv_channel.res1: One TV, one channel, infinite resentment. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.union_tv_channel.res2: A laminated voting schedule goes up by the remote. Democracy, at minimal cost.
event.union_tv_channel.title: Tv Channel
event.union_unlucky_days.desc: Unlucky days refusal. Workers have gathered outside your office.
event.union_unlucky_days.res0: Lucky charms are issued to every crew before unlucky-numbered shifts. Superstition, now a line item.
event.union_unlucky_days.res1: Unlucky-day refusals are denied outright. Attendance on the 13th mysteriously stays low anyway. Crews work 20% slower for 48 hours.
event.union_unlucky_days.res2: A shared horoscope subscription goes up in the break room. It is consulted with unsettling seriousness.
event.union_unlucky_days.title: Unlucky Days
event.union_wifi_demand.desc: WiFi in the mine shaft. The workers' committee is at your door again.
event.union_wifi_demand.res0: Fiber runs all the way down the shaft. Signal bars appear next to blast warnings on every phone.
event.union_wifi_demand.res1: No signal below ground remains policy. Lunch breaks return to actual conversation, resentfully. Union events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.union_wifi_demand.res2: WiFi arrives in the break room only. The shaft stays offline; the break room becomes very popular.
event.union_wifi_demand.title: Wifi Demand
event.unqualified_task_error.desc: A pending task requires a skill nobody on the roster has. Operations are stalled until you fix the gap.
event.unqualified_task_error.res0: An available employee gets sent to train for the missing qualification. Slower, and it fixes the gap for good.
event.unqualified_task_error.res0_alt: Nobody could be sent to train: no school teaches the skill, no one is free to go, or the course is unaffordable. Nothing was booked.
event.unqualified_task_error.res1: An outside contractor gets hired to cover the task immediately. Expensive, and it gets done today.
event.unqualified_task_error.res1_alt: The contractor could not take the job. The fee is returned and the task stays queued.
event.unqualified_task_error.res2: The blocked tasks get cancelled outright and their cost is refunded. Whatever needed doing stays undone.
event.unqualified_task_error.title: No Qualified Worker
event.weather_acid_rain.desc: Acid rain from neighboring factory. The sky has decided to complicate things.
event.weather_acid_rain.res0: A full acid-rain cleanup crew scrubs the affected area. Thorough, expensive, and effective.
event.weather_acid_rain.res1: The acid rain is ignored. Corrosion spreads across exposed equipment and exposed lungs alike. Upkeep costs 20% more for 10 days.
event.weather_acid_rain.res2: The neighboring factory gets publicly blamed for the fallout, with a little help from a friendly official.
event.weather_acid_rain.title: Acid Rain
event.weather_bad_forecast.desc: Weather forecast completely wrong. The forecast wasn't supposed to include this.
event.weather_bad_forecast.res0: Everything on the schedule gets pushed back a day. Frustrating, and considerably safer. All work on site halts for 12 hours.
event.weather_bad_forecast.res1: Operations proceed exactly as scheduled, forecast be damned. It does not go smoothly. An employee is hurt in the chaos. Crews work 20% slower for 48 hours.
event.weather_bad_forecast.res1_alt: Operations proceed exactly as scheduled, forecast be damned. It does not go smoothly. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens. Crews work 20% slower for 48 hours.
event.weather_bad_forecast.res2: A private meteorologist gets hired on retainer. Expensive, and forecasts start actually matching reality. A charge of $250 hits the books every day for 14 days.
event.weather_bad_forecast.title: Bad Forecast
event.weather_ball_lightning.desc: Ball lightning seen in pit (workers terrified). The sky has decided to complicate things.
event.weather_ball_lightning.res0: The pit is evacuated the moment the glowing orb appears. Nobody gets close enough to find out what it was.
event.weather_ball_lightning.res1: Panic spreads through the crews faster than the orb itself moves. Morale falls by 2 per hour for 12 hours.
event.weather_ball_lightning.res2: The sighting gets quietly written off as 'equipment glare' in the incident log.
event.weather_ball_lightning.title: Ball Lightning
event.weather_bird_migration.desc: Bird migration through blast zone. The forecast wasn't supposed to include this.
event.weather_bird_migration.res0: Blasting pauses entirely until the migrating flock clears the area. Slower, and genuinely good for the ecology score. Blasting is banned for 24 hours.
event.weather_bird_migration.res1: Blasting proceeds straight through the flock. Fast, cheap, and a public-relations disaster once photos surface. Lawsuit events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.weather_bird_migration.res2: Bird scarers get deployed to redirect the flock around the blast zone. A modest, workable compromise.
event.weather_bird_migration.title: Bird Migration
event.weather_debris_wind.desc: Wind shifts blast debris toward nearby village. Mother Nature has opinions about your mining schedule.
event.weather_debris_wind.res0: A full cleanup crew is sent to the village to clear the blast debris. Costly, and it earns real goodwill.
event.weather_debris_wind.res1: The debris is left where it landed. The village does not forget, and lawyers get involved shortly after.
event.weather_debris_wind.res2: The mayor receives a generous envelope. The complaint disappears faster than the wind changed direction.
event.weather_debris_wind.title: Debris Wind
event.weather_desert_snow.desc: Unexpected snow in desert mine. The weather refuses to cooperate with your blast plan.
event.weather_desert_snow.res0: An impromptu snow day is declared. Nobody in the desert has proper boots, but morale is sky-high. Morale rises by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.weather_desert_snow.res1: Work continues on the newly slick benches. Footing gets treacherous fast. An employee is hurt in the chaos.
event.weather_desert_snow.res1_alt: Work continues on the newly slick benches. Footing gets treacherous fast. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.weather_desert_snow.res2: A snowman appears at the bottom of the pit. Someone gives it a hard hat.
event.weather_desert_snow.title: Desert Snow
event.weather_double_lightning.desc: Lightning strikes same spot twice. The sky has decided to complicate things.
event.weather_double_lightning.res0: Lightning rods finally go up after the second strike makes the point unmissable.
event.weather_double_lightning.res1: The lightning-loosened rock gets blasted for free. Ecology takes a hit for the savings.
event.weather_double_lightning.res2: Nothing is fixed. Workers grow visibly spooked every time the sky darkens. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.weather_double_lightning.title: Double Lightning
event.weather_double_rainbow.desc: Double rainbow causes work stoppage for photos. Mother Nature has opinions about your mining schedule.
event.weather_double_rainbow.res0: A full stoppage lets everyone marvel at the double rainbow. Morale spikes noticeably. Morale rises by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.weather_double_rainbow.res1: Nobody is allowed to stop and look. The double rainbow passes entirely unwitnessed.
event.weather_double_rainbow.res2: The rainbow gets used as a marketing backdrop for the mine's social media. Surprisingly effective, mildly cynical.
event.weather_double_rainbow.title: Double Rainbow
event.weather_drought.desc: Drought: water supply running low. Natural forces intervene.
event.weather_drought.res0: Water trucks are brought in at real expense. Nobody goes thirsty.
event.weather_drought.res1: Water gets rationed instead. Tempers and hydration both run low. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours. The weather is held at heat wave for 36 hours.
event.weather_drought.res2: A bore well is drilled on-site. A real fix, with a real, if smaller, cost to the local water table.
event.weather_drought.title: Drought
event.weather_drought_cracks.desc: Drought cracks terrain unpredictably. Natural forces intervene.
event.weather_drought_cracks.res0: A full terrain survey maps every new crack before anyone works near them.
event.weather_drought_cracks.res1: No survey is done. A section of cracked terrain gives way without warning.
event.weather_drought_cracks.res1_alt: The ground stays put this time, cracks and all. A close call nobody wants to repeat.
event.weather_drought_cracks.res2: The worst cracks get filled and sealed before they can spread any further. Drilling is banned for 12 hours.
event.weather_drought_cracks.title: Drought Cracks
event.weather_dust_storm.desc: Dust storm reduces visibility to zero. Natural forces intervene.
event.weather_dust_storm.res0: Operations halt entirely until the dust storm clears. Costly downtime, zero blind driving. Every crew downs tools for 12 hours.
event.weather_dust_storm.res1: Work continues through zero visibility. Drivers navigate the pit essentially by memory and luck. One employee ends up in the infirmary.
event.weather_dust_storm.res1_alt: Work continues through zero visibility. Drivers navigate the pit essentially by memory and luck. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.weather_dust_storm.res2: Dust masks are handed out and work continues at a slower, marginally safer pace. Output drops 20% for 48 hours.
event.weather_dust_storm.title: Dust Storm
event.weather_early_monsoon.desc: Monsoon season arrives early. Mother Nature has opinions about your mining schedule.
event.weather_early_monsoon.res0: A proper drainage system gets installed ahead of the monsoon's usual schedule. Costly, and it holds.
event.weather_early_monsoon.res1: No drainage prep is done. Operations flood out within the first week of rain. The weather is held at heavy rain for 36 hours.
event.weather_early_monsoon.res2: Shifts get restructured around the monsoon's schedule. Awkward hours, drier feet.
event.weather_early_monsoon.title: Early Monsoon
event.weather_flash_flood.desc: Flash flood washes away stored rubble. The weather refuses to cooperate with your blast plan.
event.weather_flash_flood.res0: Stored rubble washes straight downstream into the nearby waterway. Cheap now, ugly for the ecology score. Lawsuit events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.weather_flash_flood.res1: Flood barriers hold the rubble in place. Expensive, and the waterway stays clean.
event.weather_flash_flood.res2: The flood is simply let through. Some rubble moves, some stays; nobody's fully satisfied.
event.weather_flash_flood.title: Flash Flood
event.weather_fog_lost_equipment.desc: Fog so thick equipment gets lost. Mother Nature has opinions about your mining schedule.
event.weather_fog_lost_equipment.res0: Operations shut down until the fog lifts. No visibility, no movement, no incidents. Every crew downs tools for 12 hours.
event.weather_fog_lost_equipment.res1: Work continues anyway. An excavator drives itself into a ditch nobody could see. Upkeep costs 20% more for 10 days.
event.weather_fog_lost_equipment.res2: Fog horns get mounted on every vehicle. Everyone can hear everyone else, even if they can't see them.
event.weather_fog_lost_equipment.title: Fog Lost Equipment
event.weather_frost_crack.desc: Frost fractures rock bench. The sky has decided to complicate things.
event.weather_frost_crack.res0: The cracked bench gets fully reinforced before anyone works near it again.
event.weather_frost_crack.res1: The frost damage is left alone — it turns out to make the rock easier to break apart for free.
event.weather_frost_crack.res2: The drill plan gets revised around the cracked section. Cautious, and it costs some time. Drilling is banned for 12 hours.
event.weather_frost_crack.title: Frost Crack
event.weather_frozen_fuel.desc: Cold snap freezes fuel lines. The sky has decided to complicate things.
event.weather_frozen_fuel.res0: Heated fuel lines get installed across the fleet. Expensive, and nothing freezes again this winter.
event.weather_frozen_fuel.res1: Crews thaw the lines by hand, one vehicle at a time. Slow, cold, and mildly dangerous. An employee is hurt in the chaos. The weather is held at cold snap for 36 hours.
event.weather_frozen_fuel.res1_alt: Crews thaw the lines by hand, one vehicle at a time. Slow, cold, and mildly dangerous. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens. The weather is held at cold snap for 36 hours.
event.weather_frozen_fuel.res2: Operations halt entirely until the cold snap passes. No fuel moves, nothing breaks either. All work on site halts for 24 hours.
event.weather_frozen_fuel.title: Frozen Fuel
event.weather_geomagnetic_storm.desc: Geomagnetic storm disrupts electronics. The forecast wasn't supposed to include this.
event.weather_geomagnetic_storm.res0: Faraday cages get built around the sensitive electronics just in time for the storm to pass harmlessly.
event.weather_geomagnetic_storm.res1: Nothing is protected. Sensitive electronics across the site fry simultaneously. Every crew downs tools for 48 hours.
event.weather_geomagnetic_storm.res2: Operations switch to manual controls for the storm's duration. Slower, and nothing gets fried. Crews work 20% slower for 48 hours.
event.weather_geomagnetic_storm.title: Geomagnetic Storm
event.weather_glowing_fog.desc: Fog reveals glowing outlines in the rock (fantastical). Natural forces intervene.
event.weather_glowing_fog.res0: The glowing veins get mined immediately, fog and all. Profitable, and nobody asks what caused the glow. An employee is hurt in the chaos.
event.weather_glowing_fog.res0_alt: The glowing veins get mined immediately, fog and all. Profitable, and nobody asks what caused the glow. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.weather_glowing_fog.res1: A proper geology study is commissioned instead of mining blind. Slower, and it actually explains the phenomenon.
event.weather_glowing_fog.res2: Work halts entirely out of unexplained dread. Nobody wants to go near the glowing rock.
event.weather_glowing_fog.res2_alt: The dread passes and the veins turn out to be genuinely valuable once someone finally goes back in.
event.weather_glowing_fog.title: Glowing Fog
event.weather_hailstorm.desc: Hailstorm damages vehicle roofs. The forecast wasn't supposed to include this.
event.weather_hailstorm.res0: Every dented vehicle roof gets repaired in the following days. The invoice is substantial.
event.weather_hailstorm.res1: Repairs are put off. The fleet drives around dented and rattling for weeks. Output drops 20% for 48 hours.
event.weather_hailstorm.res2: Vehicle shelters get built for next time. An upfront cost that pays for itself at the next storm. Upkeep costs 15% less for 7 days.
event.weather_hailstorm.title: Hailstorm
event.weather_heat_mirage.desc: Heat mirages confuse surveyor readings. The forecast wasn't supposed to include this.
event.weather_heat_mirage.res0: A full resurvey confirms which readings were real and which were shimmering nonsense.
event.weather_heat_mirage.res1: Drilling proceeds based on the mirage-confused readings. It goes about as well as that sounds. Crews work 20% slower for 48 hours.
event.weather_heat_mirage.res2: Surveying moves to nighttime, when the heat shimmer isn't fooling anyone's instruments.
event.weather_heat_mirage.title: Heat Mirage
event.weather_heatstroke.desc: 47°C heatstroke, workers fainting. Mother Nature has opinions about your mining schedule.
event.weather_heatstroke.res0: Cooling stations go up across the site. Fainting incidents drop sharply within a day. Everyone gets a proper rest and starts the next shift fully recharged.
event.weather_heatstroke.res1: Nothing changes. A wave of heatstroke cases sweeps through the crews by midafternoon. One employee ends up in the infirmary. Output drops 20% for 48 hours.
event.weather_heatstroke.res1_alt: Nothing changes. A wave of heatstroke cases sweeps through the crews by midafternoon. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens. Output drops 20% for 48 hours.
event.weather_heatstroke.res2: Shifts get shortened for the duration of the heat. Less output, considerably fewer people collapsing. Output drops 20% for 48 hours.
event.weather_heatstroke.title: Heatstroke
event.weather_humidity_rust.desc: Extreme humidity rusts equipment overnight. Mother Nature has opinions about your mining schedule.
event.weather_humidity_rust.res0: A full rust-treatment pass runs across every affected machine overnight.
event.weather_humidity_rust.res1: Nothing is treated. Rust spreads quietly through the fleet's joints and hinges. Upkeep costs 20% more for 10 days.
event.weather_humidity_rust.res2: Dehumidifiers are installed in the equipment sheds. A modest fix.
event.weather_humidity_rust.title: Humidity Rust
event.weather_iced_equipment.desc: Ice formation on equipment overnight. Mother Nature has opinions about your mining schedule.
event.weather_iced_equipment.res0: A dedicated de-icing crew clears every vehicle before the morning shift starts.
event.weather_iced_equipment.res1: Nothing gets de-iced. Someone slips on an icy running board before the day even properly starts. One employee ends up in the infirmary.
event.weather_iced_equipment.res1_alt: Nothing gets de-iced. Someone slips on an icy running board before the day even properly starts. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.weather_iced_equipment.res2: A fully heated garage gets built for the fleet. Expensive, and ice stops being a morning ritual.
event.weather_iced_equipment.title: Iced Equipment
event.weather_inland_waterspout.desc: Waterspout spotted near inland mine (fantastical). The weather refuses to cooperate with your blast plan.
event.weather_inland_waterspout.res0: A full emergency evacuation clears the site well before the waterspout makes landfall. All work on site halts for 12 hours.
event.weather_inland_waterspout.res1: Nobody moves. The waterspout tears straight across the pit. An employee is hurt in the chaos.
event.weather_inland_waterspout.res1_alt: Nobody moves. The waterspout tears straight across the pit. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.weather_inland_waterspout.res2: A quick 'waterspout tours' pitch gets floated to nearby visitors while the phenomenon lasts.
event.weather_inland_waterspout.res2_alt: The tour idea falls apart the moment the waterspout actually makes landfall on the pit.
event.weather_inland_waterspout.title: Inland Waterspout
event.weather_lawsuit_debris.desc: The debris you left in the village has landed on someone's desk as a lawsuit. The lawyers are circling like vultures.
event.weather_lawsuit_debris.res0: Every piece of property damage from the wind-blown debris gets paid for, in full.
event.weather_lawsuit_debris.res1: The damage gets contested in court as an act of God. It works, unexpectedly, for once.
event.weather_lawsuit_debris.res1_alt: The act-of-God defense fails badly. The court award is far larger than a settlement would have been.
event.weather_lawsuit_debris.res2: Blast shields go up to stop the debris problem. Expensive, and it helps. Hauling is suspended for 12 hours. Upkeep costs 15% less for 7 days.
event.weather_lawsuit_debris.title: Lawsuit Debris
event.weather_lightning_strike.desc: Lightning strikes near explosives magazine. The forecast wasn't supposed to include this.
event.weather_lightning_strike.res0: Lightning rods are installed around the explosive warehouse overnight. Expensive and, thankfully, effective.
event.weather_lightning_strike.res1: Nothing is done about the strike risk. The storm passes without incident, this time.
event.weather_lightning_strike.res1_alt: The magazine takes a direct hit. The explosion is heard three valleys over.
event.weather_lightning_strike.res2: Explosives are relocated to emergency storage well away from the strike zone, just in time. Blasting is banned for 12 hours.
event.weather_lightning_strike.title: Lightning Strike
event.weather_logo_cloud.desc: Cloud looks like company logo. Mother Nature has opinions about your mining schedule.
event.weather_logo_cloud.res0: The company milks the logo-shaped cloud for every ounce of free marketing it's worth.
event.weather_logo_cloud.res1: Someone declares it a bad omen. The rumor spreads faster than the cloud itself dissipates. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.weather_logo_cloud.res2: Limited-edition 'logo cloud' merchandise gets rushed into production. It sells out by lunch.
event.weather_logo_cloud.title: Logo Cloud
event.weather_meteor_shower.desc: Meteor shower visible from pit, workers want to watch. The sky has decided to complicate things.
event.weather_meteor_shower.res0: A full night-shift stargazing break is organized. Costly in lost hours, priceless in goodwill. Morale rises by 1 per hour for 24 hours. Everyone gets a proper rest and starts the next shift fully recharged.
event.weather_meteor_shower.res1: No stargazing is allowed. The meteor shower streaks by, watched by absolutely nobody on shift.
event.weather_meteor_shower.res2: A brief viewing window during the scheduled break lets a few catch a glimpse.
event.weather_meteor_shower.title: Meteor Shower
event.weather_midday_aurora.desc: Strange aurora visible at midday (fantastical, workers spooked). The sky has decided to complicate things.
event.weather_midday_aurora.res0: A spontaneous break lets everyone watch the impossible midday lights. Genuinely, inexplicably good for morale. Morale rises by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.weather_midday_aurora.res1: No explanation is offered. The unexplained lights spark genuine, lingering unease across the crews. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.weather_midday_aurora.res2: The sighting is quietly written off as 'atmospheric refraction' in the official log.
event.weather_midday_aurora.res3: A guided 'midday aurora' viewing tour launches and draws a genuine, paying crowd.
event.weather_midday_aurora.res3_alt: The tourism launch draws only a handful of confused visitors and modest, unremarkable ticket sales.
event.weather_midday_aurora.title: Midday Aurora
