event.weather_minor_tremor.desc: Minor earthquake tremor. The weather refuses to cooperate with your blast plan.
event.weather_minor_tremor.res0: A full structural inspection follows the tremor. Every bench and wall gets checked before work resumes. Blasting is banned for 12 hours.
event.weather_minor_tremor.res1: The tremor is written off as nothing. Nobody checks anything, and the cracks stay wherever they formed. An employee is hurt in the chaos.
event.weather_minor_tremor.res1_alt: The tremor is written off as nothing. Nobody checks anything, and the cracks stay wherever they formed. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.weather_minor_tremor.res2: An early-warning system gets installed for next time. A modest investment against the next shake.
event.weather_minor_tremor.title: Minor Tremor
event.weather_mudflow_thaw.desc: Warm winter melts snow, causes mudflow. The weather refuses to cooperate with your blast plan.
event.weather_mudflow_thaw.res0: Mudflow barriers go up before the thaw fully sets in. Costly, and the slope holds.
event.weather_mudflow_thaw.res1: No barriers are built. The thaw brings a proper mudslide down onto the lower benches. Hauling is suspended for 48 hours.
event.weather_mudflow_thaw.res2: Emergency drainage channels get dug just in time to redirect the worst of the meltwater.
event.weather_mudflow_thaw.title: Mudflow Thaw
event.weather_mudslide.desc: Mudslide blocks access road. The weather refuses to cooperate with your blast plan.
event.weather_mudslide.res0: A bulldozer clears the access road in a single expensive afternoon.
event.weather_mudslide.res1: Everyone waits it out. Supplies run low; patience runs lower. Hauling is suspended for 24 hours.
event.weather_mudslide.res2: The mudslide gets dynamited clear. Fast, loud, and not great for the surrounding hillside.
event.weather_mudslide.title: Mudslide
event.weather_ore_hail.desc: Freak hailstones shaped like ore chunks. The forecast wasn't supposed to include this.
event.weather_ore_hail.res0: The ore-shaped hailstones get collected and sold as a genuine curiosity. Modest profit, minor ecological eyebrow-raise.
event.weather_ore_hail.res1: Nobody collects anything. A few workers get bruised chasing free-falling rocks out of curiosity. An employee is hurt in the chaos.
event.weather_ore_hail.res1_alt: Nobody collects anything. A few workers get bruised chasing free-falling rocks out of curiosity. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.weather_ore_hail.res2: Hail shelters go up before anyone gets hurt. Nobody collects the ore hail, but nobody bleeds for it either.
event.weather_ore_hail.title: Ore Hail
event.weather_permafrost_bones.desc: Permafrost thawing reveals prehistoric bones. The weather refuses to cooperate with your blast plan.
event.weather_permafrost_bones.res0: The prehistoric bones are donated to a museum, properly documented and credited to the site.
event.weather_permafrost_bones.res1: The bones get sold quietly on the black market. Profitable, and a paleontological loss nobody will ever recover. Mafia events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.weather_permafrost_bones.res2: Work pauses for an archaeologist to properly assess the find, at real cost to the schedule. Drilling is banned for 24 hours.
event.weather_permafrost_bones.title: Permafrost Bones
event.weather_pit_fish.desc: Seasonal flooding fills pit with fish. The forecast wasn't supposed to include this.
event.weather_pit_fish.res0: An impromptu pit fishing derby draws a crowd. Fun for everyone; the ecosystem disagrees. Morale rises by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.weather_pit_fish.res1: The fish get carefully pumped out and relocated to a proper waterway. Expensive, and genuinely responsible.
event.weather_pit_fish.res2: A quick fish fry lunch uses the surplus catch. Nobody asks too many questions about where lunch came from.
event.weather_pit_fish.title: Pit Fish
event.weather_pit_flood.desc: Heavy rain floods pit, ducks move in. Natural forces intervene.
event.weather_pit_flood.res0: Pumps run around the clock draining the flooded pit. Expensive, dry, back on schedule within days.
event.weather_pit_flood.res1: A duck sanctuary sign goes up instead. Operations pause; the ducks are thrilled. All work on site halts for 12 hours.
event.weather_pit_flood.res2: Workers are told to wade through and keep working. Boots fill with water; so do the incident reports. An employee is hurt in the chaos.
event.weather_pit_flood.res2_alt: Workers are told to wade through and keep working. Boots fill with water; so do the incident reports. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.weather_pit_flood.title: Pit Flood
event.weather_pit_microclimate.desc: Microclimate forms in pit (different weather inside vs outside). The sky has decided to complicate things.
event.weather_pit_microclimate.res0: A proper study of the pit's odd microclimate gets funded. Modest cost, genuinely interesting findings.
event.weather_pit_microclimate.res1: A small greenhouse gets built to exploit the warm pocket of air. Profitable, at some cost to the surrounding ecology.
event.weather_pit_microclimate.res2: Nothing is done about it. Workers just start enjoying the oddly tropical pocket at the bottom of the pit. Morale rises by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.weather_pit_microclimate.title: Pit Microclimate
event.weather_pollen_plague.desc: Pollen season: allergies reduce workforce. Natural forces intervene.
event.weather_pollen_plague.res0: A supply of antihistamines gets distributed site-wide. Sneezing drops; morale ticks up in relief.
event.weather_pollen_plague.res1: Nothing is distributed. The workforce spends the season visibly, audibly miserable. Output drops 30% for 36 hours.
event.weather_pollen_plague.res2: Full air filtration units get installed in every shared space. Expensive, and genuinely effective.
event.weather_pollen_plague.title: Pollen Plague
event.weather_quicksand.desc: Quicksand forms in pit after rain. Natural forces intervene.
event.weather_quicksand.res0: A barrier system cordons off the quicksand patch before anyone gets close.
event.weather_quicksand.res1: The quicksand goes unmarked. A worker sinks to the waist before being pulled free. An employee is hurt in the chaos.
event.weather_quicksand.res1_alt: The quicksand goes unmarked. A worker sinks to the waist before being pulled free. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.weather_quicksand.res2: The soft patch gets filled with gravel. Solid ground again, at some cost to the surrounding soil.
event.weather_quicksand.title: Quicksand
event.weather_rainbow_pause.desc: Rainbow appears, workers stop to admire. The forecast wasn't supposed to include this.
event.weather_rainbow_pause.res0: A full rainbow break is granted. Everyone stops, stares, and comes back genuinely happier. Morale rises by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.weather_rainbow_pause.res1: Everyone is sent straight back to work. The rainbow fades unwitnessed by anyone on shift. Morale falls by 1 per hour for 24 hours.
event.weather_rainbow_pause.res2: A quick round of rainbow selfies is allowed before returning to work. Several end up online by lunch.
event.weather_rainbow_pause.title: Rainbow Pause
event.weather_sandstorm.desc: Sandstorm buries half the mine. Natural forces intervene.
event.weather_sandstorm.res0: Heavy machinery excavates the buried half of the mine back into operation within days.
event.weather_sandstorm.res1: Crews dig by hand where the machines can't reach. Slow, exhausting, and cheaper than it should be. Output drops 30% for 36 hours.
event.weather_sandstorm.res2: The buried sand gets blasted clear instead of excavated. Fast, loud, and dusty for weeks after.
event.weather_sandstorm.title: Sandstorm
event.weather_static_charge.desc: Static electricity buildup near explosives. The weather refuses to cooperate with your blast plan.
event.weather_static_charge.res0: A grounding system gets installed around the drill site before the static builds any further.
event.weather_static_charge.res1: The static buildup is ignored. Everyone hopes it dissipates on its own.
event.weather_static_charge.res1_alt: A stray spark sets off the charge early. The detonation is unplanned and considerably too close.
event.weather_static_charge.res2: Anti-static suits are issued to everyone near the drill site. A cheap, sensible precaution.
event.weather_static_charge.title: Static Charge
event.weather_sun_glare.desc: Sun glare blinds excavator operator. The forecast wasn't supposed to include this.
event.weather_sun_glare.res0: Tinted windshields go on every excavator cab. The glare stops being a hazard by lunchtime.
event.weather_sun_glare.res1: Nothing changes. The operator squints through the glare and hopes for the best. Crews work 20% slower for 48 hours.
event.weather_sun_glare.res2: Comically oversized sunglasses get issued instead of real fixes. They work, somehow, and morale ticks up.
event.weather_sun_glare.title: Sun Glare
event.weather_suspiciously_perfect.desc: Perfect weather streak makes workers paranoid. Natural forces intervene.
event.weather_suspiciously_perfect.res0: Free paranoia counseling is offered to anyone unnerved by the good weather. It helps, oddly.
event.weather_suspiciously_perfect.res1: Nothing is done. Superstitious panic spreads about the weather being 'too good to be true'. Morale falls by 2 per hour for 12 hours.
event.weather_suspiciously_perfect.res2: A small shrine to the weather gods appears near the break room. Nobody admits to building it.
event.weather_suspiciously_perfect.title: Suspiciously Perfect
event.weather_sweaty_explosives.desc: Humidity causes explosives to sweat. Natural forces intervene.
event.weather_sweaty_explosives.res0: Climate-controlled storage gets built for the explosives. Expensive, and the sweating problem simply stops.
event.weather_sweaty_explosives.res1: The sweating is ignored. The humid stock sits exactly where it was, quietly becoming less stable.
event.weather_sweaty_explosives.res1_alt: The unstable stock detonates on its own. The blast is heard well beyond the site boundary.
event.weather_sweaty_explosives.res2: The affected stock gets replaced outright. Costly, but the risk leaves with the old batch. Explosives cost 15% less for 7 days.
event.weather_sweaty_explosives.title: Sweaty Explosives
event.weather_temp_inversion.desc: Temperature inversion traps dust in pit. Mother Nature has opinions about your mining schedule.
event.weather_temp_inversion.res0: Dust suppression systems run at full capacity until the inversion clears. Costly, and breathable.
event.weather_temp_inversion.res1: Nothing is done. The trapped dust settles into every set of lungs on site. The weather is held at cloudy for 36 hours.
event.weather_temp_inversion.res2: Respirators are handed out for the duration. Basic, cheap, and it helps more than expected.
event.weather_temp_inversion.title: Temp Inversion
event.weather_tidal_bore.desc: Tidal bore floods coastal mine. Mother Nature has opinions about your mining schedule.
event.weather_tidal_bore.res0: Tidal walls go up before the surge arrives. Expensive, and the coastal pit stays dry.
event.weather_tidal_bore.res1: No walls are built. The tidal bore floods the pit exactly as feared. The weather is held at heavy rain for 36 hours.
event.weather_tidal_bore.res2: A designated surf break gets marked off instead of fighting the tide. Unconventional, and it works out fine.
event.weather_tidal_bore.title: Tidal Bore
event.weather_tornado_warning.desc: Tornado warning: evacuate or risk it?. The sky has decided to complicate things.
event.weather_tornado_warning.res0: A full site evacuation clears everyone out well ahead of the funnel cloud. Every crew downs tools for 12 hours.
event.weather_tornado_warning.res1: Nobody moves. The tornado tracks elsewhere, this time.
event.weather_tornado_warning.res1_alt: The tornado tears straight through the site. The damage bill is enormous.
event.weather_tornado_warning.res2: A partial evacuation clears the most exposed crews while a skeleton team keeps things running. Output drops 30% for 36 hours.
event.weather_tornado_warning.title: Tornado Warning
event.weather_tourist_sunrise.desc: Sunrise creates perfect mine tourism lighting. The sky has decided to complicate things.
event.weather_tourist_sunrise.res0: Guided sunrise mine tours launch and sell out immediately. Beautiful light, considerably more foot traffic. An employee is hurt in the chaos.
event.weather_tourist_sunrise.res0_alt: Guided sunrise mine tours launch and sell out immediately. Beautiful light, considerably more foot traffic. Nobody is healthy enough to get hurt, so the injury never happens.
event.weather_tourist_sunrise.res1: The opportunity passes unused. The sunrise remains beautiful and entirely unmonetized.
event.weather_tourist_sunrise.res2: A designated photo spot gets marked for the sunrise shot. Modest revenue, minimal disruption.
event.weather_tourist_sunrise.title: Tourist Sunrise
event.weather_wind_paperwork.desc: Wind blows away blast plan paperwork. The weather refuses to cooperate with your blast plan.
event.weather_wind_paperwork.res0: Blast plans get reprinted and laminated on the spot. A minor cost for a major relief.
event.weather_wind_paperwork.res1: The crew blasts from memory instead of waiting for reprints. Confidence is high; accuracy is not guaranteed. Lawsuit events become 2x as frequent for 7 days.
event.weather_wind_paperwork.res2: Plans move to a digital tablet system on the spot. Wind stops mattering to paperwork, at least for today.
event.weather_wind_paperwork.title: Wind Paperwork
event.weather_wind_turbine.desc: Wind turbine opportunity on ridgeline. The weather refuses to cooperate with your blast plan.
event.weather_wind_turbine.res0: A full wind farm goes up on the ridgeline. Expensive, and it quietly powers half the site. Upkeep costs 15% less for 7 days.
event.weather_wind_turbine.res1: The opportunity is passed over entirely. The ridgeline stays exactly as it was.
event.weather_wind_turbine.res2: A single turbine gets installed as a modest test. Small, quiet, and a decent first step.
event.weather_wind_turbine.title: Wind Turbine

ui.level_end.defeat.bankruptcy.body: Cash sat under $5,000 for a hundred hours straight. A receiver arrived this morning, walked the site once, and used the word "salvage" four times.

ui.level_end.defeat.arrest.tip: Exposure builds from mafia activity, not from bribery itself. The HUD shows an exposure pip once it reaches seventy-five percent and you get one warning toast; at ninety percent the arrest happens immediately, and a sudden jump past ninety skips the warning.
Ecology sat at zero for a hundred fifty hours straight. Inspectors have fenced the pit, and a local school has adopted the tailings pond as a science project.
The ecology bar turns critical below 20 in the HUD. From true zero, the shutdown clock runs a hundred fifty hours — recovering even slightly at any point resets it.

With no Living Quarters on site, employees have nowhere to recover and their well-being sinks faster. Build a Living Quarters so they can rest. Once well-being hits zero, the crew walks out after {hours} hours.
ui.level_end.defeat.worker_revolt.tip.mo: Shifts and housing are in place, yet well-being still drained to zero. Check the rest threshold in the site policy, bed capacity and overcrowding in your Living Quarters, and recent incidents hurting morale. Once well-being hits zero, the crew walks out after {hours} hours.

tutorial.title: Tutorial
tutorial.step2: Hire a Surveyor to scan the terrain for ore deposits. Open the Crew panel and click Hire.
tutorial.step3: Now perform a seismic survey to reveal ore locations underground.
tutorial.step_overlaytoggle.title: Toggle the Confidence Overlay
tutorial.step_overlaytoggle: The colored overlay showing survey confidence doesn't have to stay on. Click the toggle in the Survey panel — or press O — to switch it off, or back on, whenever you like.
tutorial.step4: Hire a Driller to prepare blast holes for mining. Check the Crew panel.
tutorial.step_livingquarters: Watch the well-being score up top — fatigue drags it down, and a crew that never rests eventually revolts. Build Living Quarters now, before the drilling and blasting ahead wears your crew down.
tutorial.step_earlypolicy: The default policy already sends tired crew to rest — select Continuous under Shift schedule and apply it, so tired crew get pulled off the line automatically before they collapse.
tutorial.step5: Open the Blast Workshop panel and place drill holes where ore was detected.
tutorial.step6: Set explosive charges on your drill holes to prepare for the blast.
tutorial.step8: The blast fires by itself once the zone is clear. Watch the rock break, then close the Blast Report.
tutorial.step9: Keep an eye on your scores: well-being, safety, ecology and neighbour relations. Hover over or click the score bars at the top of the screen to inspect them.
tutorial.step10: Random events will occur during gameplay. Respond to keep your mine running smoothly.
tutorial.step11: Hire a Manager to negotiate better contracts.
tutorial.step13: Hire a Driver to operate your vehicles. Open the Crew panel and hire a Driver.
tutorial.step14: Buy a vehicle from the Fleet panel.
tutorial.step15: Build a Freight Warehouse to store mined ore and fragments for logistics.
tutorial.step_drivingcenter: The first blast leaves boulders too big to haul. Build a Driving Center so a driver can learn to run a rock fragmenter.
tutorial.step_trainfragmenter: Train your driver on the Rock Fragmenter licence at the Driving Center you just built. Open the Crew panel.
tutorial.step_buydrillrig: Buy a Drill Rig from the Fleet panel.
tutorial.step_buyrockdigger: Buy a Rock Digger from the Fleet panel.
tutorial.step_haul: Your crew handles hauling on its own now: a qualified driver boards a free Debris Hauler, drives it to the nearest debris, and brings it back to storage. Open the Fleet panel and watch it happen.
tutorial.step_sellore: Accept an offer for ore you have stored (greyed-out offers ask for ore the pit does not contain), then deliver it once your hauler brings it to storage. You may need several rounds — the warehouse only holds so much at once.
tutorial.step16: Deliver ore to fulfill your active contract. Use logistics to complete deliveries.
tutorial.step17: Monitor your cash flow: income, expenses and profit. Click your balance at the top of the screen to open the Finances panel.
tutorial.step19: Watch your employees' fatigue. Open the Crew panel from the toolbar to check their needs.
tutorial.step23: You've completed the tutorial! You're ready to mine. Good luck.
